The test image shows two tomato stems split longitudinally, revealing brown internal vascular/pith discoloration, with deteriorated roots attached. This is the classic diagnostic presentation of a vascular wilt disease. Key features: stems cut lengthwise, brown streaking throughout internal tissue, no white mycelium or sclerotia visible.

Top candidates: **Verticillium_Wilt** (brown vascular discoloration in stems cut lengthwise) and **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** (pith discoloration). I'll use my 1 reference image on Verticillium Wilt.

The Verticillium Wilt reference shows leaf symptoms (V-shaped yellowing), but the test image shows stems split open — which is the diagnostic method for vascular wilts. The knowledge base explicitly states Verticillium Wilt presents with "brown vascular discoloration visible when stems are cut lengthwise," which exactly matches the test image's brown internal tissue discoloration in longitudinally split stems with deteriorated roots.

No white mycelium, sclerotia, or streaming bacterial exudate visible, ruling out Southern Blight, Sclerotinia, and Southern Bacterial Wilt streaming test. The internal brown vascular/pith discoloration in cut stems is the hallmark of Verticillium Wilt.
